contract.headline: A 48h timelock covers contract-upgrade (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, UPGRADER_ROLE). asset-permission (MINTER_ROLE) has NO established delay — timelock: unresolved. The delay protects the code and not the supply.
contract.headline_basis: Derived from the layer rows below, not authored here, so it changes when the walk changes.
contract.method_note: Replaced a v1.7 generator row that read topology: unknown, m: 4, timelock: unresolved. security_analyst's generator is iced; on their own coverage audit only 36.5% of generated rows were trustworthy.
unresolved: ethereum asset-permission: MINTER_ROLE holders NOT established by this repo. riskAnalyst assets/reusd-re.md walked three undelayed paths (an ERC1967Proxy/InsuranceCapitalLayer, an InstantRedemption whose authority slot leads to an OZ AccessManager, and a BurnWithFromMintTokenPool whose owner() is the 3-of-5 Safe) and reports all three terminating at Safe 0x8eec1061…fbad with getTargetAdminDelay 0. THAT IS THEIR WALK, NOT OURS — the addresses are truncated in their file so a direct hasRole check had no candidates, and a RoleGranted/RoleRevoked enumeration over the last 400,000 blocks TIMED OUT on three public endpoints. Unresolved, not zero.

ethereum contract-upgrade: PROPOSER/CANCELLER role holders on timelock 0x69ddea33…fca93 not enumerated here. Safe 0x8eec1061…fbad is 3-of-5 (measured) and is reported by riskAnalyst as sole PROPOSER, with an independent CANCELLER EOA at nonce 0; neither role assignment was read from the timelock by this repo.
arbitrum/base/avalanche: same-address absence confirmed (code size 0). A deployment at a different address was NOT searched for.

forceNAVUpdate path: 0xe888df3218e070fae8d90d2ba6fcac5520217484 (632B, nonce 1) carries both setSharePrice and forceNAVUpdate selectors and answers no standard interface. Whether it IMPLEMENTS or CALLS them needs disassembly, which was not done. It is also not expressible in this schema — see the `parameter` open item in registry/incidents.md.
walk_notes: ⚠️⚠️ THIS FILE HAS A LIVE PUBLIC CONSUMER — ADDED 2026-08-31.
backing-monitor's `tools/emit_axis5.py` reads it FRESH ON EVERY SYNC and renders
axis 5 of the reUSD dashboard from it. There is no stored copy anywhere, by
design (our invariant 1), which means:
* editing this file CHANGES A PUBLISHED PAGE within one sync;
* deleting or retracting it makes axis 5 fall back to "Not assessed" rather
than serving a withdrawn walk — the generator emits nothing and does not
fail their sync;
* `observed_at` below is the AXIS CLOCK on that page. Their generator REFUSES
TO EMIT if it is absent, rather than substituting a run time. Do not touch
it without re-reading the chain — a laundered date renders as a fresh
measurement to a reader who has no way to check.
* the header comment block IS PART OF THE OUTPUT. Paragraphs marked with ⚠️
are surfaced on the page, selected by that marker. Write them as if a
reader outside this repo will see them, because one will.
⚠️ If reUSDe (or any other slug) is ever walked, backing-monitor's SLUG_TO_FILE
needs one line added or the file will land and render nothing. Tell them; do not
assume a new file is picked up.
✅ HAND-WALKED 2026-08-30, NOT GENERATOR OUTPUT. This file deliberately does NOT
carry the TRUST WARNING banner the generator files carry — it replaces a v1.7
generator file that held ONE layer, `topology: unknown`, `m: 4` and
`timelock: unresolved`, which was materially worse than what riskAnalyst's
assets/reusd-re.md was already citing FROM it.
⚠️ THE OLD FILE'S SINGLE LAYER CONFLATED TWO AUTHORITIES, and riskAnalyst named
it first: "LAYER LABEL FITS ONLY PART OF WHAT IS FILED HERE — MINTER_ROLE is not
a contract-upgrade authority." Correct. Mint lives in `asset-permission` (USDai
is the worked case, keys [BRIDGE_ADMIN_ROLE, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE]). Split here so
"2 days on the code" and "no delay on the supply" are two rows rather than one
row hiding the second inside the first.
VERIFICATION TRAIL (this repo, ethereum, 2026-08-30, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com):
token 0x5086bf35…0c72  name() "Re Protocol Deposit Token"  supply 201,084,062.66
EIP-1967 impl 0xb5276c43…21d4 (6,498B); beacon slot 0x0; ADMIN SLOT 0x0
upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes) PRESENT / upgradeTo(address) ABSENT  -> OZ v5 UUPS
owner() transferOwnership() admin() proxiableUUID() ALL REVERT       -> not Ownable
grantRole(bytes32,address) PRESENT                                   -> AccessControl
hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, timelock 0x69ddea33…fca93) = TRUE
hasRole(UPGRADER_ROLE,      timelock 0x69ddea33…fca93) = TRUE
hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN/UPGRADER/MINTER, Safe 0x8eec1061…fbad) = FALSE  <- flows via the timelock, not direct
timelock.getMinDelay() = 172800 (2d); MINIMUM_DELAY() and MIN_DELAY() BOTH REVERT
Safe 0x8eec1061…fbad getThreshold()=3 getOwners()=5
control: hasRole(MINTER_ROLE, 0x…dEaD) = FALSE
⚠️ CHAIN COVERAGE IS ETHEREUM-ONLY, AND THAT IS A BOUNDED CLAIM. The token
address has code size 0 on arbitrum, base and avalanche. PegTracker's backing
snapshot describes the asset as "Ethereum primary; also Arbitrum, Base,
Avalanche", so a deployment at a DIFFERENT address on those chains is NOT
excluded — it was not searched for. Same-address absence only.
⚠️ THE UPGRADE DELAY HAS NO FLOOR. getMinDelay() is 172800 but no MINIMUM_DELAY
constant exists, so the delay is reducible by whoever can schedule against the
timelock's own admin. Reading delay_current alone overstates the protection —
the same shape audits/held-layer-delay-canceller.yaml found on every timelock
row it examined.
